newsitem.title: USA: Parke-Davis withdraws some flu vaccines.
newsitem.headline: Parke-Davis withdraws some flu vaccines.

text.p: The Parke-Davis division of Warner-Lambert Co has voluntarily recalled six lots of its influenza vaccine because a strain of the vaccine may in time lose some of its potency, Parke-Davis said on Thursday.
Spokesman Jeff Baum said there was nothing unsafe about the vaccine and the recall was "strictly precautionary."
The recall numbered about 1.8 million doses, representing some four percent of all the vaccine distributed by drug-makers to U.S. care givers.

Baum said that one of the strains in the three-strain vaccine was found to lose potency before the end of its one-year shelf life. But he said that people who have had the Parke-Davis vaccine would not not need an additional dose.
Three lots of about 300,000 doses each were recalled on November 1 and three more on November 6, he said.
